title: Things to Do in Kolhapur: Mahalaxmi Temple, Palaces, Panhala & Fiery Food
seoTitle: Things to Do in Kolhapur: Temples, Forts & Food | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Kolhapur: the Mahalaxmi (Ambabai) Temple, New Palace and its museum, Rankala Lake, Panhala Fort, Jyotiba Temple, the Town Hall Museum, wrestling at a talim, Kolhapuri chappals and saaj jewellery, and tambda-pandhra rassa.
dek: A historic Maratha capital in southern Maharashtra, known for its goddess temple, royal palace, wrestling culture, leather chappals and very spicy food.
searchIntent: Pilgrims and travellers planning one or two days in Kolhapur, often on the way to Goa or the Konkan.
intro: Kolhapur, on the Panchganga river in southern Maharashtra, was the capital of a Maratha princely state founded by Tarabai in the early 18th century. Its ruler Shahu Maharaj (1874–1922) was a pioneering social reformer, and the city has a strong tradition of wrestling, music and cinema.

The things to do in Kolhapur include darshan at the ancient Mahalaxmi Temple, the New Palace and its royal museum, evenings at Rankala Lake, a drive up to Panhala Fort and the Jyotiba Temple, and shopping for Kolhapuri chappals and traditional jewellery. The food, especially the red and white mutton curries, is famous and fiery.
One or two days is enough. October to February is the most comfortable time.
quickAnswer: Tour the New Palace and Shahu Chhatrapati Museum
Watch wrestlers train at a talim
Buy Kolhapuri chappals and saaj jewellery

items.name: Visit Mahalaxmi Temple
body: The Mahalaxmi (Ambabai) Temple, in the heart of the old city, is one of the Shakti Peethas and among the most important temples in Maharashtra. Its stone structure dates in part to the Chalukya period. During the Kiranotsav, on a few days in January or February and in November, the setting sun's rays reach the idol.

The temple's outer walls are covered with carvings, and the complex includes smaller shrines to other deities. The streets around it are full of stalls selling flowers, bangles, kumkum and the green saris that devotees offer to the goddess.

items.name: Visit the Jyotiba Temple
body: The Jyotiba Temple, on a hill about 17 km north-west, is dedicated to a local form of Shiva. During its spring fair, devotees throw pink gulal, turning the hill pink.

items.name: See Kaneri Math
body: The Siddhagiri Gramjivan Museum at Kaneri Math, about 12 km away, has life-size sculptures recreating traditional Indian village life, a popular outing for families.

items.name: Tour the New Palace
body: The New Palace, built of black stone between 1877 and 1884 in a blend of Indo-Saracenic styles, is still the residence of the royal family. Part of it houses the Shahu Chhatrapati Museum, with arms, hunting trophies, costumes and royal belongings.

items.name: See the Town Hall Museum
body: The Town Hall Museum, in a colonial building with gardens, has archaeological finds from the Brahmapuri excavations, paintings and weapons.

items.name: Watch wrestlers at a talim
body: Kolhapur is famous for kushti, traditional Indian wrestling. Wrestlers train in mud pits at talims (akhadas) such as Motibag. Visitors can sometimes watch early-morning training with permission, and bouts are held at the Khasbag stadium.

items.name: Watch sunset at Rankala Lake
body: Rankala Lake, on the western edge of the city, has a promenade with food stalls and horse rides, a small temple in the water and the Shalini Palace on its shore. It is the city's favourite evening spot.

items.name: Explore Panhala Fort

image.alt: Walls of Panhala Fort near Kolhapur
image.caption: Panhala Fort

body: Panhala, about 20 km north-west, is one of the largest forts in the Deccan, with granaries, gates and walls on a plateau. It is famous for Shivaji's escape from a siege in 1660, covered by Baji Prabhu Deshpande's last stand at Pavankhind. Panhala is also a small hill station.

Look for the Sajja Kothi pavilion, where Shivaji is said to have planned his escape, the three-storey Andhar Bavdi (hidden well) and the Teen Darwaza gate. The ramparts give views across the Warna and Kasari valleys.

items.name: Visit Dajipur and Radhanagari
body: The Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary, including Dajipur, about 80 km away, protects forests with Indian gaur (bison) and many birds and butterflies.

items.name: Eat tambda and pandhra rassa
body: Kolhapuri mutton is served with two curries: tambda rassa, a fiery red gravy, and pandhra rassa, a mild white gravy made with coconut milk. Kolhapuri misal and the local bhakri are also famous. Spice levels are high; ask for milder versions if needed.

items.name: Buy Kolhapuri chappals and saaj
body: Kolhapuri chappals, hand-crafted leather sandals with a GI tag, are sold in the Chappal Line market. Kolhapuri saaj, a traditional gold necklace, and jaggery from the region are other classic buys.

items.name: October to February
body: The most pleasant time, with Navratri celebrations at the Mahalaxmi Temple in autumn.

items.name: March to May
body: Hot days; the Jyotiba fair takes place in spring.

items.name: June to September
body: Heavy monsoon rain on the Sahyadri side, green landscapes and flooding risk along the Panchganga.

byTraveller.text: Mahalaxmi at dawn, Jyotiba and the evening aarti.
New Palace museum, Rankala Lake, Kaneri Math and Panhala.
A Kolhapuri mutton thali, misal for breakfast and jaggery to take home.
Break the Pune–Goa drive in Kolhapur for a night: temple in the evening, mutton thali for dinner and Panhala at dawn.

oneDay: Visit the Mahalaxmi Temple early, then tour the New Palace museum. After a Kolhapuri lunch, drive to Panhala Fort for the afternoon, and return to Rankala Lake for sunset and street food.
tips: Kolhapur has a railway station and a small airport; Pune is about four hours by road.
The temple is crowded on Fridays and during Navratri.
Spice levels are high; ask for less if needed.
Buy chappals from established shops for genuine quality.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Kolhapur?
faqs.a: Visit Mahalaxmi Temple, tour the New Palace, watch sunset at Rankala Lake, explore Panhala Fort, visit Jyotiba, watch wrestlers train and eat Kolhapuri food.
The Mahalaxmi Temple, Kolhapuri chappals, spicy mutton curries, wrestling and its royal heritage.

faqs.q: How far is Panhala from Kolhapur?
faqs.a: About 20 km, around 45 minutes by road.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Kolhapur?
When is Kiranotsav at Mahalaxmi Temple?
faqs.a: On a few days around late January or early February and again in November, when the setting sun's rays fall on the idol.
